name: eBay used bare A100 80GB PCIe cards (the mainstream ex-datacenter consumer path)
price_basis: USED / Pre-Owned, bare A100 80GB **PCIe** card. $12,099.00 = the lowest listing whose own title states PCIe (NOT the $10,449.95 entry, whose title says 'SXM4 Module' -- see FORM-FACTOR NOTE below; an earlier revision of this record wrongly attributed that SXM4 listing to this PCIe record). Genuine PCIe 80GB cards ranged $12,099.00-$21,995.00 across the same page: HPE P46814-001 $16,999.00, Cisco UCSC-GPU-A100-80 $19,500.00, Dell 575TK $20,830.18, A100X 80GB converged $21,995.00. Two-card lots: $24,198.00 for 2x SXM4, $42,270.00 for 2x PCIe. Warranty: none from NVIDIA. All figures captured 2026-10-03 as ASKING prices, not sold.
notes: FORM-FACTOR CORRECTION (2026-10-03, parent agent): this record previously carried price_usd 10449.95 with accelerator_ids nvidia-a100-80gb-pcie. That figure came from a listing whose own title reads 'A100 80GB SXM4 Module' -- an SXM module, not a PCIe card. The same $10,449.95 listing is correctly recorded as SXM in `ebay-used-accelerator-market`. SXM modules are unusable without an HGX carrier, so quoting them as the price of a PCIe card understated the real entry point by ~14%. price_usd now uses the lowest self-identified PCIe listing ($12,099) and status is `contested` because the band is thin. Separately, the median of a wider n=17 A100 80GB asking band (which mixes SXM4 modules and SXM4-to-PCIe conversions) is $21,995 -- see `used-a100-80gb-pcie-market`, whose band deliberately does not separate the two form factors. Do not average the two records. This is the channel most buyers actually mean by 'a used A100', and the price structure across it is highly informative. (1) The whole used A100 80GB market on eBay is THIN: only 27 used items, of which just one is 'Certified refurbished' and one 'Very Good - Refurbished'. There is essentially no manufacturer-certified refurb channel for A100 at scale - it is all one-off private-party pulls. (2) OEM-branded pulls carry a visible premium over generic ones: HPE P46814-001 at $16,999 and Cisco UCSC-GPU-A100-80 at $19,500 versus generic NVIDIA-branded at $12,099-$12,500, a roughly 35-60% premium that buys OEM firmware/support history rather than better silicon. (3) EXPLICIT DEFECT PRICING, the most useful single datapoint in this slice: an A100 80GB PCIe at $12,500.00 has 'ECC Error' in its own title. A known-fault 80GB A100 costs about the same as a clean bare SXM4 module, i.e. roughly 40% less than the $21,139 clean PCIe ask. That gap is the market price of burn-in risk. (4) RISK - retrofit adapters are a trap: an 'H100 SXM5 to PCIe adapter 80gb 96gb' is listed at $899.00 (open box, ships from China) and an 'A100 40GB SXM2-to-PCIe Test-Version Card with RTX 4090 Cooling Kit' at $6,160.00. These SXM-to-PCIe conversions are uncooled or oddly-cooled engineering artefacts, not production parts, and the thermal and firmware story is not something a buyer can verify before the HBM hits its limit. (5) Export regime: SXM listings carry explicit 'US only / Requires Compliance Approval' terms.
